issue.title: Check our Delta at D 12-30 with the RT prototype and a multiprecision LU

milestone.title: G8 · Other paths
milestone.description: Alternatives to our formulation and methods (the RT variables of arXiv:2611.07007, Fourier speed, low D from first principles), the large-D expansion to higher orders, and the complex scalar.

issue.body:
**What.** Add a double-double or arb LU to `solver/rt/rt_run.py` and continue the RT prototype from D 10 to 30 on two grids (N_t 32 with N 81 and N 101). Recommended by #91's subagent.

**Why.** An independent check of our Δ by a different formulation and discretization, in the range where the published values have only six decimals. At D = 4 and 10 the prototype already agrees with hp to 1e-12 (notes/RT_FORMULATION.md).

**Acceptance (can fail).** |Δ_RT − Δ_hp| < 1e-10 at D 15, 20 and 30 on both grids; the two grids agree with each other to 1e-10; `--mutate=coef` moves Δ by more than 1e-6 and exits 1.

**Depends on.** #91 (merged, 973a3da).

comments.body: started, a subagent of the coordinator on mac (Apple M5), in its own git worktree, 2 processes at nice 10. WIP branch wip/i105, raw folder I105-mac/. It posts its own progress and closing summary here; the coordinator closes the issue after review.

Progress (subagent, mac). The multiprecision Jacobian solve is built and passes its planted test: `solver/rt/rt_mpsolve.py`, Newton with the arb residual (192 bits) and each step by flexible GMRES in arb, preconditioned by the f64 LU of the f64 Jacobian applied with double-double triangular solves (multidouble's `dd_dot` per row).

Planted system, kappa = 1e20 exactly (L = 1500): error 9.3e-40 against the criterion 1e-30, 4 Newton steps of 11 products each; the f64 LU alone leaves an error of 66. `--mutate=f64apply` (error 64) and `--mutate=lowprec` (error 5e15) exit 1. The two designs tried first failed and are recorded: GCR with f64 triangular solves (error 47), and the explicit f64 inverse applied in double-double (80 products per step, the cap).

Measured costs at L = 9185 (32x81): an arb residual 0.11 s, the f64 Jacobian 4.5 s, its LU 1.8 s. A dense arb LU would take about an hour (I91's 3.8e-9 s/L^3), and multidouble's dense dd LU (`dd_solve`, 2.0e-10 s/L^3) 154 s per factorization with no reuse of its factors. The GMRES route needs only matrix-vector work per product.

Now running the pilot: D = 10 on 32x101 from I91's 48x81 state, then one Newton solve at D = 12. The continuation on both grids follows. Branch wip/i105 (54b95d1), raw folder I105-mac/.

Progress (subagent, mac). Pilot done (`I105-mac/pilot/`, raw commit 032b2fd). On 32x101, one Newton solve at D = 12 from the D = 10 solution converged in 8 steps (residual 6.2e-2 to 1.6e-42), with Delta_RT - Delta_hp = -5.8e-17, in 150 s. The f64 preconditioner is rebuilt after large steps: without the rebuilds a preconditioner from 8e-2 away needed 62 to 76 GMRES products per step instead of 10. The 1/2-step continuation 10 to 12 lands on the same Delta to 20 digits.

The two continuations (32x81, L = 9185; 32x101, L = 11425) are running, 2 processes at nice 10, about 2.3 GB each. So far, Delta_RT - Delta_hp:

| D | 32x81 | 32x101 |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | +1.08e-12 | -3.0e-17 |
| 12 | -7.8e-13 | -5.8e-17 |
| 13 | +8.6e-13 | |
| 14 | +4.5e-12 | |
| 15 | +1.13e-11 | |

On 32x81 the error grows by about 1.5x per half unit of D, so that grid will probably miss the 1e-10 acceptance at D 20 and 30. If it does, I'll report it with its numbers, not loosen it. The LU pivot ratio (an estimate of kappa) is 1e15 to 1e17 from D = 11 on. Per D step, 5 Newton steps of 12 to 22 GMRES products each, about 1.5 min (N 81) to 2.5 min (N 101). Expected end of both runs: about 07:15 UTC.

**Results summary (subagent, mac), for the coordinator's review.** The issue stays open with its labels unchanged.

The acceptance is met on 32x101 and missed on 32x81. On 32x101 the RT prototype reproduces our Delta at D 15, 20.043653 and 29.984746 to 1.1e-16, 1.7e-16 and 3.2e-16. On 32x81 it misses 1e-10 at D 20.04 and 29.98, at 1.4e-10 and 1.2e-9, so the two grids also disagree there. The cause is the truncation of 81 Chebyshev points, which grows with D, not the solve. A 32x121 control lands within 2.3e-22, 1.7e-20 and 5.3e-18 of ours at the three D.

**Method.** `solver/rt/rt_mpsolve.py` (new) runs Newton with the arb residual at 192 bits. Each step is solved in arb by flexible GMRES, preconditioned by the f64 LU of the f64 Jacobian, whose triangular solves run in double-double (one multidouble `dd_dot` per row). The products J u are exact central differences of the quadratic arb residual. It is wired in as `rt_run.py --solver mp`. A dense extended-precision LU was rejected on measured cost: per Newton step it would take an estimated 223 s / 420 s in double-double (`dd_solve`) and 50 / 98 min in arb, at L = 9185 / 11425.

**What ran and its exits** (raw folder `I105-mac/`):

| run | exit |
|---|---|
| planted, kappa = 1e20 exactly, L 1500 (`rt_mpsolve.py --selftest`) | 0. Error 9.3e-40 against the criterion 1e-30, 4 Newton steps of 11 products; the f64 LU alone leaves 66 |
| planted `--mutate=f64apply` / `--mutate=lowprec` | 1 / 1 (errors 64 and 5e15) |
| planted variants: GCR + f64 solves (the first design) | 1 (error 47). FGMRES + f64 solves passes with 45-59 products; the explicit f64 inverse hits the cap of 80 |
| planted, in-place LU (the controls' code), and its mutations | 0; 1, 1 |
| pilot, 32x101: D 10 re-solve, then one Newton solve at D 12 from it | 0, 0. D 12 converged in 8 steps, 150 s, -5.8e-17 from hp |
| continuation 32x81, D 10 to 30 in steps of 1/2 | 1 (checks at 20.04 and 29.98) |
| continuation 32x101, D 10 to 30 | 0 |
| `--mutate=coef` at D 15 and 29.98 (32x81 states) | 1, 1. Delta moved by 3.75e-4 and 3.06e-3 |
| resolution controls: 48x101 and 32x121 at the three D | 0 (all) |
| `rt_grids.py` 81 vs 101 / 121 vs 101 / 121 vs 101 with `--mutate=shift` | 1 / 0 / 1 |
| `rt_mp_cost.py` on both grids / its `--mutate=perturb` | 0, 0 / 1 |

**Delta_RT - Delta_hp** (`rt_grids.py`, `I105-mac/accept_grids.log`). hp is `hp/data/delta_all.csv`, double-double rows 15.0 (up), 20.043653 (up2) and 29.984746 (up6). These are the exact D hp solved, since it rounds D to six decimals.

| D | 32x81 | 32x101 | 81 - 101 | 48x101 | 32x121 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | +1.13e-11 | -1.13e-16 | +1.13e-11 | -1.13e-16 | -2.3e-22 |
| 20.043653 | +1.40e-10 FAIL | -1.68e-16 | +1.40e-10 FAIL | -1.68e-16 | +1.7e-20 |
| 29.984746 | +1.24e-9 FAIL | +3.20e-16 | +1.24e-9 FAIL | +3.21e-16 | +5.3e-18 |

These are measured differences between two discretizations, not bounds.

- N_t 32 is not the limit: 48x101 differs from 32x101 by at most 1e-19.
- The 1e-16 offset of 32x101 is its own xi truncation, as 32x121 shows.
- Along the path the 32x81 error is -1.1e-12 at D 10, changes sign between 12.5 and 13, then reaches 1.4e-10 at 20 and 1.24e-9 at 30.

**Cost.** One Newton step took 13-18 s (32x81) and 19-35 s (32x101) from D 15 to 30, the arb parts on one core. One step of 1/2 in D took 1.4-2.3 min and 2.3-4.3 min. The whole continuations took 70 and 117 min. The products dominate: each costs 0.35 / 0.48 s and is two arb residuals. The count per Newton step grows about 2 per unit of D, from 7 at D 10 to about 50 at D 30 on 32x101.

**Discrepancies (reported, not fixed).**

- Sections 5(3) and 5b of the note price the RT Newton by a dense extended-precision LU, at hours per step, and the verdict leans on it ("on 14 to 24 times our unknowns in a dense LU"). This solve factors only in f64 and needs 13-35 s per step up to D 30. What still grows with D is the product count and the Chebyshev N that holds Delta.
- The f64 LU pivot ratio, 5e12 to 1.4e17, saturates and is not kappa. Kappa on the resolving grids past D 10 was not measured.
- hp's stated err of 1e-16 is conservative here: 32x121 agrees to 2e-22, 2e-20 and 5e-18. At D 29.98 that matches hp's own dDelta_est of 5.4e-18.
- The main runs used a rebuild rule (commit a9cb86b) that rebuilt the preconditioner on most steps past D 21, which cost 14 and 30 min. That affects cost only. The relative rule (1090efb) fixes it for later runs.
- The first check in `rt_mp_cost.py` compared against J64 and was wrong. It now checks the backward error against the factors: 3.5e-36 and 2.9e-37.

**For #106.**

- The solver carries over (`--grids 40x79`). The in-place LU holds one Jacobian copy, 1.0 GB at L 11201.
- `--max_products` must be raised: at 2 per unit of D the count reaches 80 near D 45.
- Plan about 2-4 min per step of 1/2 at L about 11k, growing with D.
- The measured N = 81 collocation truncation, extended at its D 20-30 growth (an extrapolation), would reach the size of EEG's 5e-7 departure between D 50 and 60.

**Commits.** wip/i105 head 3e371f2 (code 54b95d1 ... fb8a012, 8a109a7, 5b5e2e9, b5b260a; note section 9). The continuations ran at a9cb86b and the controls at 1090efb and later. Raw-data repository: I105-mac at 6c9d697 (earlier 032b2fd, a9bd961, c006a57).

**Recommended tasks**

1. **A double-double product J u for the RT prototype.**
   - What: compute the inner GMRES products by a vectorized double-double linearized residual instead of two arb residuals, with the outer Newton residual kept in arb.
   - Why: the products are most of every Newton step (40-50 per step at D 30, 0.48 s each), and #106 needs about 60 steps per grid from D 30 to 60.
   - Acceptance: on 32x101 at D 20.043653 from the stored state, Delta equals the arb-product run's to 1e-25, and the seconds per Newton step are at most half of 19 s. The planted kappa 1e20 test still passes. A mutation (one derivative-matrix entry in the product perturbed by 1e-12) must raise the products per step by more than 50% or fail the planted test.
   - Depends on: #105.
2. **Smallest singular value of the resolving RT grids at D 20-30.**
   - What: sigma_min of J at the 32x101 solutions at D 20.04 and 29.98, by inverse iteration with newton_mp's FGMRES solve (no dense arb), at 192 and 320 bits.
   - Why: the f64 pivot ratio saturates, and section 4's kappa laws stop at D 10 on resolving grids. The product count suggests the weak directions grow by about 2 per unit of D.
   - Acceptance: the two precisions agree to 1e-6 relative. The same code recovers the planted system's 1e-20 to 1e-6. Its 64-bit mutation must fail.
   - Depends on: #105.
3. **Amend #106's commands.**
   - What: start from `I105-mac/cont/cont_32x101_D30.0000_32x101.npz` with `--solver mp --max_products 160`.
   - Why: the D 10-30 path is done, and the cap of 80 binds near D 45.
   - Acceptance: #106's own.
   - Depends on: #105.

Coordinator review. I reran `rt_grids.py` from the raw records: 32×101 against 32×121 exits 0, `--mutate=shift` exits 1, and 32×81 against 32×101 exits 1, the miss as reported. Merged into main as d967f7a. Verdict: the RT prototype on 32×101 reproduces hp's Δ at D 15, 20.04 and 29.98 to 3e-16, and on 32×121 to 5e-18, an independent check of our values by a different formulation and discretization. 32×81 misses 1e-10 at D ≥ 20 from Chebyshev truncation, which bears on #106.
Discrepancy 1 is accepted: #91's cost argument priced a dense extended-precision LU, and this solver takes 13–35 s per step. That part of RT_FORMULATION.md's verdict no longer stands. #145 measures whether the rest still does. The recommended tasks are #143 (double-double products), #144 (κ on the resolving grids), #145 (to D 60–100, the cost growth) and the #106 command amendment. Discrepancy 6, the outdated AGENTS.md in the worktree, is fixed on main (58b048c).
